source.title: Long time behaviour of one facilitated kinetically constrained models: results and open problems

accepted.question_text: Consider the one-dimensional Fredrickson-Andersen one-spin facilitated model (FA-1f) on the lattice Z with infection density q in (0,1), where a site may update only when at least one nearest neighbor is infected, and let π be the Bernoulli product equilibrium measure with density q of infected vertices. Is it true that for every such q, every initial distribution ν that almost surely contains at least one infected vertex, and every local observable f depending on finitely many sites, the law of the process converges locally to equilibrium in the sense that lim_{t→∞} |E_ν(f(η(t))) − π(f)| = 0?
accepted.context_brief: FA-1f convergence to equilibrium from any nontrivial initial state

evidence.quote: A second basic question is to determine under which conditions on q and on the initial distribution ν, the law of the process at time t converges to the equilibrium measure π as t → ∞. Natural choices for ν are the Bernoulli product measure µq0 with q0 > 0, q0 ≠ q or the Dirac mass on the configuration with a single infection at the origin. For FA-1, it is natural to conjecture the following. Conjecture 1. For any q ∈ (0, 1) and any function f depending on the state of finitely many vertices lim t→∞ |Eν(f(η(t))) − π(f)| = 0, (1.1) provided that ν(∃ an infected vertex) = 1.

For the FA-1f process the constraint satisfies cx(η) = 1{ηx−1+ηx+1̸=2}. Informally, FA-1f can be described via its so-called graphical representation as follows: each vertex x ∈ Z is equipped with a unit intensity Poisson process... if the current configuration has at least one empty site among the nearest neighbours of x, we update the state of x

accepted.question_text: In the same one-dimensional FA-1f model on Z with infection density q in (0,1) and equilibrium measure π, suppose the initial law ν has exponentially decaying probability of containing no infected site in a centered interval, in the sense that there exists κ > 0 such that ν(no infected vertices in [−ℓ,ℓ]) = O(e^{−κℓ}) for all sufficiently large ℓ. Does this stronger nondegeneracy assumption imply that, for every q > 0, the convergence of local observables to equilibrium is exponentially fast in time?
accepted.context_brief: Exponential relaxation under an exponential-tail hypothesis

evidence.quote: The next obvious question concerns the speed of relaxation to the reversible measure π under some condition on ν stronger than just the a.s. existence of some infection. Conjecture 2. If there exists κ > 0 such that ν(no infected vertices in [−ℓ, ℓ]) = O(e−κℓ) for all ℓ > 0 large enough then for all q > 0 the convergence in (1.1) is exponentially fast.
For the FA-1f process the constraint satisfies cx(η) = 1{ηx−1+ηx+1̸=2}.

accepted.question_text: Let a kinetically constrained model be given, let E denote the set of stable configurations for its associated bootstrap percolation dynamics, let π be the Bernoulli product reversible measure of the model, and for each β in E let π_β be the measure obtained by conditioning π on the event {BP(η)=β}. Must every stationary measure µ of the kinetically constrained model admit a decomposition µ = ∫_E π_β dµ*(β) for some probability measure µ* on E? In other words, are stationary measures exactly mixtures of the equilibrium product measure conditioned on the bootstrap-percolation stable configuration?
accepted.context_brief: Structure of stationary measures for general KCMs

evidence.quote: In view of the discussion above and of Theorem 2.13, we propose the following conjecture. Conjecture 3. Let µ be a stationary measure of a KCM. Then there exists a probability measure µ∗ on E such that µ = ∫E dµ∗(β)πβ, where πβ is given by the measure π conditioned on the event {BP(η) = β}.
We say that a configuration η is stable for the bootstrap percolation if BP(η) = η, and denote the set of stable configurations by E.
For a stable configuration β, let πβ be the measure π conditioned on the event {BP(η) = β}.

accepted.question_text: For the Fredrickson-Andersen one-spin facilitated model in dimension d ≥ 2 at infection density q > 0, consider the finite-volume process on the box Λ_n^d with a choice of boundary condition or conditioning that makes the chain ergodic. Is the mixing time of this ergodic finite-volume chain always linear in n for every q > 0?

evidence.quote: Finally, a related question in higher dimensions is the scaling with n of the mixing time of the (ergodic) chain on Λdn. The conjecture is a linear scaling for all values of q > 0, but, once more, that has been proved only for q large enough [10].

However, due to the presence of constraints, the logarithmic Sobolev constant is either infinite for the process on the whole lattice, or very large (i.e. Θ(n)) for the chain on the finite set Λn = {0, 1, . . . , n} with either appropriate infected boundary conditions ensuring irreducibility or conditioned on having at least one infection.
